summary: You take nine East Asia content courses: EASTASN 330 and eight from the approved list, each at least 3 units and passed with a B or better, plus any additional coursework to reach 46 units. Every course must be letter graded when that option exists and numbered 100 or above (200 or above for HISTORY); language courses below 100, EFS language classes and more than 6 units of EASTASN 300 do not count toward the 46 units. You check by hand that 30 of the content units are at the graduate level, that three content courses share a department or theme, petitioned content courses (at most three) and a P in a GSB or Law course, that each course is an academic content course (not an activity or studio course), the program and thesis proposals, the thesis presentation, the thesis, the language requirement and the 3.0 GPA.

M3ZrqQ45.why: "Students must complete a minimum of 46 units at Stanford (no transfer credits accepted), comprised of: Minimum nine East Asia content courses ... B. Additional coursework as necessary to reach the minimum 46 units". An overview whose parts are now rules: the 46 units (the Bulletin's unit minimum and the floor on block mAbEGmbJ), the content courses (Hr8TpL87, Ay6UiIkD), the same-department-or-theme rule and the additional coursework (added rules).

Hr8TpL87.why: "EASTASN 330 counts toward the nine content courses." "Must be taken for a letter grade (if available) and completed with a B or higher."

Ay6UiIkD.why: "Minimum nine East Asia content courses ... Includes EASTASN 330 core course ... Are on the approved East Asian Studies course lists below, or have been approved by petition (maximum three petitions), Are a minimum of three units ... Are taken for a letter grade (if available) and completed with a B or higher (P or higher in GSB courses and Law courses)." EASTASN 330 is one of the nine, so eight come from the list. Petitioned courses and a P in a GSB or Law course are moved in by hand; "at least 30 units of which must be at the graduate level" is not checked.

ggy1gIJr.why: "The following program milestones are additionally required for all students: Program Proposal ... Thesis Proposal and Literature Review ... Thesis Presentation: Once during their time in the MA program, students are required to present their thesis project at a public presentation."

h8KjQB3a.why: A policy, not a requirement: "Petition to Count Course toward the Nine Content Course Requirement ... Directed Reading Course Approval Policy". The Bulletin stored it as a requirement to take EASTASN 300. Its 6-unit cap on EASTASN 300 is on the additional coursework rule.

EEBlt5SF.why: "Students must submit a master's thesis representing a substantial piece of original research with a minimum of 10,000 words in the main body". A requirement, not an overview.

r17oHuUN.why: "Students must demonstrate proficiency in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean language equivalent to Stanford's first three full years of language training. This requirement may be fulfilled by one of three methods: Completing the third-year course sequence at Stanford; Examination ...; By possessing a degree from a university where the language of instruction is in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean." The third-year courses are not named, so it is checked by hand.

node.name: Additional coursework toward 46 units (letter graded, 100 or above; HISTORY 200 or above)

add.why: "B. Additional coursework as necessary to reach the minimum 46 units for the degree must meet the following criteria: Taken for a letter grade, At least level 100 or above (above 200 for HISTORY courses)" and "A maximum of 6 units of EASTASN 300 may be applied to the 46 required degree units." Optional because the content courses may reach 46 units alone; it counts toward the 46-unit floor on the block.
